Although it reports task-evoked voxelwise activation analyses, acquisition covered only ten slices centered on the amygdala, and the authors note restricted brain coverage; a whole-brain task map is therefore not demonstrated (I3 not met). It includes non-ROI voxelwise activation results, so E1 does not apply.

I2 is not demonstrated: the paper reports a mean age and SD but does not establish that at least one healthy group falls within ages 18–65; at full text, an unestablished inclusion criterion is recorded as not_met.

The study uses fMRI during social emotion recognition in healthy adults, but its acquisition covers a restricted slab centered on the amygdala rather than providing whole-brain evidence; I3 is not demonstrated.

The study uses fMRI during social-personality judgments (I1) in 20 healthy participants whose mean age is 18.7 (I2). Whole-brain task-evoked evidence is not demonstrated: the reported maps are corrected within a priori ROIs (I3 not met), meeting the ROI-only exclusion (E1).

The study uses fMRI during a social competition task and reports whole-brain group-level task contrasts in healthy volunteers. However, it reports only a mean age and standard deviation, not that participants were aged 18–65; age eligibility is therefore not demonstrated (I2). E4 is unclear because the text does not establish that all participants were outside the eligible range.

The paper reports fMRI during a social threat/empathy task (I1) and group-level whole-brain task contrasts (I3). The participants are adults, but the full text does not establish that they are healthy; healthy-adult eligibility was therefore not demonstrated (I2). This is an exclusion at full text because I2 is not met.

Social-related fMRI task and healthy adults aged 18–45 are demonstrated (I1, I2). The whole-brain findings are Group × Redistribution interactions, not a clearly identified unmasked healthy-group task effect (I3 not met; E3 met).
The study uses fMRI for social self-attribute evaluations and reports whole-brain task contrasts, but the full text does not establish that the analyzed adult sample was healthy (I2 not_met).

This empirical fMRI study examines social gestures in a healthy sample and reports whole-brain task-evoked group results (I1–I3). However, the sample includes participants younger than 18, and the results do not report a separate eligible adult subgroup; E4 is met.

The study uses fMRI during a social dilemma task and includes adult participants. However, the reported whole-brain maps compare prosocial and proself subgroups or test their interactions; no unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy group is reported (I3 not met; E3 met).

The study uses task fMRI in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task effects (I2, I3), but its task tests levels of abstraction in action concepts rather than social-related processing as defined by I1. Exclude on I1.

The study uses fMRI during social exclusion and reports whole-brain task effects, but participant ages are not reported, so the required healthy adult age range was not demonstrated (I2). The article itself is complete.

The study uses fMRI during a social face-perception task (I1) and includes healthy adults aged 18–65 (I2). However, its whole-brain analyses report only neural responses associated with individual differences, not an unmasked healthy-group task effect; I3 is therefore not demonstrated and E3 applies. It includes whole-brain analyses beyond ROI-only results and is not solely connectivity or resting-state research (E1–E2 not met).

The fMRI task examines social exchange (I1), and the paper reports a whole-brain task-evoked conjunction analysis (I3). However, the reported sample ages are means and standard deviations, not evidence that any healthy group is within the required 18–65 range; under full-text rules, I2 is not demonstrated and the study is excluded. Age limits are not stated clearly enough to determine E4.

The study examines prosocial learning with fMRI in healthy adults (I1, I2 met), but the reported task-evoked findings are small-volume-corrected ROI results; a qualifying healthy-group whole-brain map is not demonstrated (I3 not met; E1 met).

The study examines fMRI responses during social processing and reports whole-brain task analyses. However, the younger group spans ages 17–27, and the paper does not report results separately for a healthy subgroup restricted to ages 18–65; I2 is therefore not demonstrated.

The study uses fMRI for empathy for pain and includes healthy adult participants, but its whole-brain results are stress-versus-control group contrasts, not an unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy/control group (I3). It therefore meets E3.

I1 and I3 are met: the study uses fMRI for social facial-emotion processing and reports whole-brain task-related analyses in the healthy sample. I2 is not_met because the full text reports a mean age but does not demonstrate that participants were within the required 18–65 range; under full-text rules, an unproven inclusion criterion is not_met.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related biological-motion judgment task and includes healthy adults. Although the methods mention whole-brain contrasts, the reported inferential analyses and coordinates are restricted to predefined MNS and MS masks, so no whole-brain task map is demonstrated (I3 not met; E1 met).

The study examines collaborative social communication with fMRI in healthy adults aged 18–33 and reports whole-brain results. Those results are contrasts between retrieval conditions, not a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy group; I3 is therefore not demonstrated.

The study uses fMRI to examine mothers’ responses to their own child’s facial emotions, and includes healthy control mothers. However, it does not demonstrate an unmasked whole-brain task effect from the healthy group: the reported CON familiarity effect remained after masking by the CON > ELM interaction. I3 is not met and E3 applies.

I1 is met: the study uses dual fMRI during cooperative and competitive social interaction. I3 is met: it reports group-level whole-brain task-response analyses. I2 is not demonstrated: although participants’ mean age is reported, the full text does not establish that they were healthy adults; under full-text rules, this inclusion criterion is not met.

The paper reports whole-brain fMRI task activation for dynamic facial-expression processing, but does not demonstrate that the healthy participant group falls within the required age range: it reports a mean age and SD without an age range or confirming that participants were adults (I2 not demonstrated). E4 is unclear because ages outside the range are not established.
